name: Ushuaia and Tierra del Fuego
region: Tierra del Fuego, southern tip of Argentina
tagline: The southernmost city in the world, ringed by snow-capped mountains on the Beagle Channel, gateway to Antarctica, penguin islands and the last stretch of the Pan-American Highway.
highlight: Sailing the Beagle Channel past sea lions and the red-and-white Les Éclaireurs lighthouse, with the mountains behind.
shortDescription: A port at the end of the world, with Beagle Channel cruises, Tierra del Fuego National Park, the End of the World Train, penguins and the departure point for Antarctic cruises.
metaDescription: An Ushuaia travel guide: the Beagle Channel and Les Éclaireurs lighthouse, Tierra del Fuego National Park, the End of the World Train, Isla Martillo penguins, Antarctica cruises, best time and a three-day plan.

goodFor: Wildlife, boat trips, hiking, Antarctica departures

image.alt: The town of Ushuaia beside the Beagle Channel with snow-capped mountains behind

intro: Ushuaia, on the Beagle Channel at the southern tip of South America, is widely called the southernmost city in the world, at 54° 48' south, although some tiny settlements in Chile lie further south. It lies at the foot of the Martial Mountains, on the large island of Tierra del Fuego, which is shared by Argentina and Chile, and it was founded in 1884, first as a mission and then as a penal colony. Its former prison, now a museum, is one of its main sights.

The city now lives on tourism, fishing and its role as the main departure port for cruises to Antarctica, which sail from about November to March. A visit here does not need an Antarctic trip, though, since the surroundings are spectacular: boat trips on the Beagle Channel pass sea lions, cormorants and lighthouses, penguin colonies can be visited on Isla Martillo and Estancia Harberton, and Tierra del Fuego National Park offers forest and lake walks and the end of Ruta 3, the road that begins in Buenos Aires.

The climate is cool and changeable even in summer, and the light is long and strong, with sunset after 10pm in December. It is at its best from November to March, and winter offers skiing and quiet. It is a place of dramatic landscapes and the thrill of standing near the end of the world.

whyVisit.intro: Ushuaia is a unique destination at the edge of the map, with wildlife and wilderness at its doorstep.

points.title: The end of the world
points.text: The southernmost city, where the Andes plunge into the sea.

points.title: Beagle Channel cruises
points.text: Sea lions, cormorants, lighthouses and mountain views.

points.title: Penguins
points.text: Magellanic and Gentoo penguins on Isla Martillo, one of the few places where you can walk among them.

points.title: Gateway to Antarctica
points.text: Most Antarctic cruises leave from here.

attractionsIntro: Most sights are on the water or in the nearby national park.

attractions.name: The Beagle Channel and Les Éclaireurs Lighthouse

image.alt: The red-and-white Les Éclaireurs lighthouse on a rock in the Beagle Channel

attractions.text: The strait named after Darwin's ship, with boat trips to sea lion colonies, bird islands and the picturesque red-and-white lighthouse, often called the lighthouse at the end of the world.
attractions.tip: Book a morning departure, and dress warmly.

attractions.name: Tierra del Fuego National Park

image.file: File:Lago Acigami, Tierra del Fuego National Park, Argentina.jpg
image.alt: Lago Acigami in Tierra del Fuego National Park with forest and mountains

attractions.text: The country's southernmost national park, with coastal trails, southern beech forests, peat bogs and the sign marking the end of Ruta 3, at Lapataia Bay, 3,000 km from Buenos Aires.

attractions.name: The End of the World Train

image.file: File:El Tren del Fin del Mundo - Train of the End of the World (38885899470).jpg
image.alt: The steam train known as the End of the World Train running through Tierra del Fuego

attractions.text: A narrow-gauge steam railway that follows the route once used by prisoners to bring timber, through the national park.

attractions.name: Isla Martillo penguin colony
attractions.text: An island with Magellanic and Gentoo penguins, visited on small-boat tours, and one of the few places where visitors can land and walk among penguins.
attractions.tip: Book with a licensed operator, and go from October to March.

attractions.name: The Maritime and Prison Museums
attractions.text: The former prison houses museums on the penal colony, maritime history and Antarctic exploration.

attractions.name: Martial Glacier
attractions.text: A short chairlift and walk above the town to a small glacier, with views of the channel.

thingsToDoIntro: Ushuaia is a place for water, walks and a sense of adventure.

thingsToDo.title: Sail the Beagle Channel
thingsToDo.text: See sea lions, seabirds and lighthouses.

thingsToDo.title: Walk among penguins
thingsToDo.text: A guided landing on Isla Martillo.

thingsToDo.title: Ride the End of the World Train
thingsToDo.text: A steam train through the forest.

thingsToDo.title: Eat king crab
thingsToDo.tip: Try it in a local restaurant.

foodIntro: Ushuaia's food is seafood and Patagonian lamb, at high prices.

foods.name: Centolla (king crab)
foods.text: The sweet meat of the southern king crab, served hot or cold.

accommodation.intro: Stay in the town centre, or in a lodge outside for views.

areas.name: Town centre
areas.text: Hotels and hostels along San Martín Street.

areas.name: The hills above town
areas.text: Lodges with panoramas of the channel.

gettingThere.intro: Ushuaia is reached by air, or by long road trips through Chile.

options.text: Direct flights from Buenos Aires (about 3 hours 30 minutes), El Calafate and other cities.

options.mode: Bus and ferry from Río Gallegos
options.text: A long journey via Chile and the Strait of Magellan.
Some Antarctic and Patagonian cruises start and end here.

gettingAround.intro: The town is small, and tours and taxis reach the sights.

options.text: To the national park and trailheads.

bestTime.headline: November–March
bestTime.summary: Ushuaia has a cold, windy, changeable oceanic climate, with cool summers and cold winters.

seasons.text: Long days, mild weather and the busiest season.
Beautiful autumn colours and fewer visitors.
Cold and snowy, with skiing and few visitors.

bestTime.avoid: Winter for boat trips and penguins, since services close.

days.morning: The End of the World Train.

days.title: Penguins
days.morning: A trip to Isla Martillo or Harberton.

tipsIntro: A few tips help you prepare.
tips: Bring layers, waterproofs, gloves and a hat, even in summer.
Book penguin landings and the train ahead.
Check the weather and wind for boat trips.
Bring sunscreen, since the sun is strong.
Book Antarctic cruises many months ahead, or look for last-minute deals in Ushuaia.
Allow extra time for flights, which are prone to delays.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Ushuaia?
Is it really the southernmost city?
faq.a: It is widely called so, though small settlements in Chile, such as Puerto Williams, lie further south.
Yes, on Isla Martillo and at Estancia Harberton, from about October to March.

faq.q: What is the best time to visit?
Can I go to Antarctica from Ushuaia?
faq.a: Yes, cruises leave from about November to March. Book well ahead.
Yes, particularly for accommodation, food and cruises.
